replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics has always been my closest friend since childhood. As a retired man from vocational training, I found solace in its logical structure. Gardening taught me patterns, and painting helped me visualize geometry. I enjoy solving puzzles and appreciate how math connects to everyday life, like budgeting or understanding weather patterns.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Not really. My experience with math was positive from school days, and I’ve used it practically in gardening and cooking. I see anxiety as a sign of overcomplication. When I feel unsure, I break problems into smaller steps—like checking measurements in my garden or calculating paint needed for a wall. Math is a tool, not a stressor.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Last year, I tried a simple math app for gardening calculations. It helped me figure out how much soil to buy based on garden size. The app was easy to use and gave clear steps. I didn’t need to worry about complex algorithms—it was just practical math for my hobbies. No anxiety, just helpful.

replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduces data dimensions by finding directions (principal components) that capture most variance.
